item.text:
**Verdict**  
Mixed, leaning **no**. Sharif’s 2024 government did back some targeted welfare and protection measures, especially social protection, food security, and minority-rights rhetoric, but the broader record still shows exclusion, coercive policing, abusive evictions, and weak protection for vulnerable groups in practice.

**Positive Evidence**
- **Pakistan: IMF Reaches Agreement on Economic Policies for 37-month Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-07-12 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff  
  Claim: the program explicitly targeted stronger, more inclusive growth and included expanded BISP social protection plus higher education and health spending. This is the clearest sign that the government treated vulnerable groups as a policy priority. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: World Bank Approves $535 Million for Crisis-Resilient Social Protection and Climate-Smart Growth in the Livestock and Aquaculture Sectors** | World Bank | 2024-06-20 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/20/pakistan-world-bank-approves-535-million-for-crisis-resilient-social-protection-and-climate-smart-growth-in-the-livestoc  
  Claim: Pakistan was strengthening its social protection system for poor and vulnerable households, with explicit support for female farmers and food security. This is strong positive evidence for women, the poor, and climate-vulnerable communities. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **National Minorities Day being observed today** | Radio Pakistan | 2024-08-11 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/11-08-2024/national-minorities-day-being-observed  
  Claim: state media framed minority rights as part of socio-economic inclusion and equal citizenship. This supports a welfare-and-inclusion reading, though it is still mostly rhetorical. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **Government of Pakistan says it strengthened measures for vulnerable groups** | Press Information Department | 2024-12-10 | https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27376  
  Claim: the government said it had taken legislative steps for vulnerable groups, strengthened commissions for women, children, and human rights, and improved minority-rights protection. This is the best institutional evidence of a pro-vulnerable-groups posture. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **World Bank Reaffirms Support for Pakistan’s Recovery** | World Bank | 2024-04-02 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/01/pakistan-implementing-an-ambitious-credible-and-clearly-communicated-economic-reform-plan-critical-for-robust-recovery-p  
  Claim: the World Bank tied recovery to restoring stability for households and highlighted social pressures and fragility. This is weaker than the IMF item, but it supports the idea that the government was at least trying to stabilize conditions for vulnerable people. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **World Report 2024: Pakistan** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/pakistan  
  Claim: after prison-health reporting, Sharif ordered sanitation and health-care measures in Lahore Central Prison and promised wider prison reforms. This is a narrow but concrete welfare-related intervention affecting incarcerated and otherwise vulnerable people. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9

**Negative Evidence**
- **Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent  
  Claim: HRW said the government clamped down on media, opposition, and NGOs, and that weak social security undermined rights to health, food, and an adequate standard of living. That cuts against a real priority on vulnerable groups. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: Authorities must end escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/  
  Claim: Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and blocked religious rites for Ahmadis while authorities failed to ensure safety. This is strong evidence against prioritizing a persecuted minority. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/  
  Claim: the government rushed through harsh protest restrictions rather than aligning rules with human-rights standards. That suggests control and deterrence mattered more than welfare for marginalized publics. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-27 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/  
  Claim: Amnesty described deaths, mass detentions, and a communications blackout during the Islamabad crackdown. This is direct counterevidence to a vulnerable-groups-first governing style. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: Abusive Evictions Target Urban Poor** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-28 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/28/pakistan-abusive-evictions-target-urban-poor  
  Claim: HRW reported forcible evictions of low-income residents, shop owners, and street vendors without adequate notice, compensation, or resettlement. This is strong negative evidence on treatment of the poor and marginalized urban communities. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **HRCP general body calls for consensus on civilian autonomy, climate justice and land rights** | Human Rights Commission of Pakistan | 2024-11-17 | https://hrcp.wittywebsolutions.com/hrcp-general-body-calls-for-consensus-on-civilian-autonomy-climate-justice-and-land-rights-2/  
  Claim: HRCP said the state had prioritized authority over rights and should instead focus on health, education, workers, peasants, and women. This is a strong domestic civil-society critique against a vulnerable-groups-centered state. IDs: 6B.3, 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

**Search Gap**
- I found **better evidence for social protection and minority/women framing** than for actual improvements in access for **children, the elderly, disabled people, or poor regions**.
- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of broad, measurable service delivery gains across all vulnerable groups.
- The best positives are mostly **program commitments or targeted interventions**; the best negatives are **repression, evictions, and discriminatory treatment**.
